The invention is directed to a thermochromic color-memory composition capable of reversibly changing color in response to temperature while also memorizing and retaining selected color states. More specifically, the composition can interchangeably memorize a colored state and a decolored state, or different visible states, and maintain those states over a practical temperature range. This makes it possible to achieve stable and reliable color-memory performance, rather than a simple temporary thermochromic color change.

Because of these effective color-memory properties, the composition is suitable for use in a wide variety of fields. It may be applied to products where temperature-responsive indication, decorative effects, security features, educational tools, writing instruments, toys, textiles, packaging, or other functional color-changing applications are desired. Its ability to retain a color state after a temperature change broadens its usefulness in applications requiring persistent visual information or reversible display characteristics.

The invention further provides a thermochromic color-memory microcapsule pigment in which the thermochromic color-memory composition is encapsulated. By enclosing the composition within microcapsules, the pigment can be more easily incorporated into inks, coatings, plastics, fibers, paints, printing materials, and other host materials. Encapsulation also helps protect the active thermochromic components and improves handling, dispersion, durability, and practical applicability.

The thermochromic color-memory composition contains, as essential components, an electron-donating color-developing organic compound, an electron-accepting compound, and a specific ester compound. The electron-donating color-developing organic compound serves as a chromogenic material capable of developing color through interaction with the electron-accepting compound. The electron-accepting compound functions as a developer that interacts with the electron-donating compound to produce a colored state.

The specific ester compound acts as a reaction medium for controlling the color-forming reaction between the electron-donating and electron-accepting components. By regulating the interaction between these components in response to temperature, the ester compound enables the composition to exhibit thermochromic behavior as well as color-memory performance. As a result, the composition can achieve reversible color change and stable retention of the selected color state, making it highly useful as a thermochromic color-memory material.

The invention relates to a thermochromic color-memory composition and to a microcapsule pigment containing that composition. More particularly, the invention provides a reversible thermochromic system capable not only of changing color in response to temperature, but also of memorizing and retaining either a colored state or a decolored state over a practical temperature range after the temperature stimulus has been removed.

The composition includes, as essential components, an electron-donating color-developing organic compound, an electron-accepting compound that reacts with the electron-donating compound to produce color, and a reaction medium composed of a specified ester compound. By appropriately selecting and combining these components, the composition exhibits a clear and controllable color-change behavior. The electron-donating compound functions as the color former, while the electron-accepting compound serves as the developer. The ester reaction medium regulates the interaction between these two components and determines the temperature range in which coloration, decoloration, and color retention occur.

A key feature of the invention is that the composition can reversibly assume different visual states depending on its thermal history. When heated or cooled beyond predetermined temperatures, the composition changes between a colored state and a substantially colorless or differently colored state. Once the composition has reached one of these states, it can retain that state even after being returned to ordinary ambient temperature. In this way, the composition demonstrates a “color-memory” effect, allowing the displayed color to be fixed until another temperature stimulus is applied.

The invention also provides a microcapsule pigment in which the thermochromic color-memory composition is enclosed within a capsule wall. Encapsulation improves handling, stability, dispersibility, and compatibility with various binders, resins, inks, coatings, and molded materials. The microcapsules protect the active thermochromic components from external influences and make it possible to incorporate the color-memory function into many types of products without impairing the reversible color-changing performance.

Because the composition is able to control both color development and color retention effectively, it is useful in a wide range of applications. For example, it may be used in writing instruments, printing inks, paints, coatings, plastics, fibers, toys, novelty goods, temperature indicators, security markings, educational materials, and decorative articles. Products incorporating the composition can display stable colors under normal conditions while allowing the color to be changed or erased by heating or cooling.

Thus, the invention provides a practical thermochromic color-memory material that combines reversible color change with reliable memory and retention of the selected color state. Through the use of the specific ester reaction medium together with an electron-donating color-developing compound and an electron-accepting compound, the composition achieves stable, interchangeable thermochromic color behavior suitable for diverse industrial and consumer applications.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract in English for a thermochromic color-memory composition and microcapsule pigment, using the standard “[Problems]” and “[Solution]” format and describing components (a), (b), and an ester compound of Formula (1).
counterfactuals.output:
[Problems]  
To provide a thermochromic color-memory composition that exhibits a clear reversible color change with excellent color density, sharpness, and color-memory performance, and that can stably retain either a colored state or a decolored state over a practical temperature range. Also, to provide a microcapsule pigment containing the composition and suitable for use in writing instruments, printing inks, coatings, molded articles, fibers, and other thermochromic products.

[Solution]  
A thermochromic color-memory composition comprising:  
(a) an electron-donating color-developing organic compound;  
(b) an electron-accepting compound capable of developing color by reacting with component (a); and  
(c) a reaction medium containing an ester compound represented by Formula (1), the ester compound controlling the color-developing and decoloring behavior of components (a) and (b) and imparting thermal hysteresis thereto.  

By using the ester compound of Formula (1) as at least part of the reaction medium, the composition exhibits a reversible thermochromic behavior in which color development and decoloration occur at different temperatures, thereby enabling a color-memory effect. The composition may be enclosed in a microcapsule to form a thermochromic microcapsule pigment, in which the shell wall protects the thermochromic color-memory composition and improves dispersion stability, durability, and processability in various media.

**Problem:**  
Conventional thermochromic color-memory compositions often exhibit insufficient color density, unstable hysteresis behavior, poor long-term storage stability, or limited control over the temperature range in which color development and decolorization occur, particularly when used in inks, coatings, molded articles, or encapsulated systems.

**Solution:**  
The invention provides a thermochromic color-memory composition comprising (i) an electron-donating color-developing organic compound, (ii) an electron-accepting compound capable of reacting therewith to develop color, and (iii) an ester compound serving as a reaction medium. By selecting the ester reaction medium to control the reversible association and dissociation between the electron-donating and electron-accepting compounds, the composition exhibits stable thermochromic hysteresis, retains either a colored or decolored state over a predetermined temperature range, and provides improved color-memory performance suitable for incorporation into writing instruments, printing inks, coatings, resins, fibers, and other thermochromic articles.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate the English abstract section of a patent for a thermochromic color-memory microcapsule pigment, including the object of the invention and the solution with substituent ranges for Formula (1).
counterfactuals.output:
## Abstract

**Object:**  
The present invention provides a thermochromic color-memory microcapsule pigment having excellent color-density, sharp and reversible thermochromic behavior, and a large hysteresis width, whereby either a colored state or a decolored state can be stably retained over a practical temperature range even after removal of a heating or cooling stimulus.

**Solution:**  
The thermochromic color-memory microcapsule pigment comprises microcapsules encapsulating a reversible thermochromic composition containing:  
(a) an electron-donating color-forming organic compound;  
(b) an electron-accepting compound; and  
(c) a reaction medium comprising at least one ester compound represented by Formula (1):

\[
\mathrm{R^{1}COO-(CH_{2})_{m}-OOCR^{2}}
\]

wherein **R¹** and **R²** are each independently a linear or branched alkyl group or alkenyl group having **5 to 21 carbon atoms**, and **m** is an integer of **2 to 12**. The components are enclosed within a microcapsule wall to form a pigment having an average particle diameter suitable for incorporation into inks, coatings, resins, writing instruments, printing materials, textile treatments, and molded articles. The ester compound of Formula (1) adjusts the melting/crystallization behavior of the reaction medium, thereby imparting a color-memory effect in which the pigment exhibits a colored state below a lower transition temperature and a decolored state above an upper transition temperature, while maintaining either state in an intermediate temperature region.
